name: Levetiracetam
summary: Levetiracetam (Keppra) is an FDA-approved seizure medicine that is sometimes used off-label in psychiatry for mood, aggression and behavior problems.
description: Levetiracetam is an anticonvulsant (seizure medicine). It attaches to a protein in nerve cells called SV2A, which changes how nerve cells release chemical messengers and calms overactive nerve signals. It is FDA-approved for seizure disorders. It has also been used off-label (not FDA-approved for this use) in psychiatry to help stabilize mood and reduce aggression and behavior problems, especially in people with neurological conditions.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Levetiracetam is an anticonvulsant that binds to synaptic vesicle protein 2A (SV2A), modulating neurotransmitter release and reducing neuronal excitability. It is FDA-approved for seizure disorders but has been used off-label in psychiatry for mood stabilization, aggression, and behavioral dysregulation, particularly in neurological conditions.
